Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 12, verses 1–3:

Volume four of Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir Kalam al-Rabb al-Mannan, by its compiler, the one poor before his Lord, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Abd Allah al-Sa'di, may Allah forgive him, his parents, and all Muslims. Amin.

This surah is Meccan.

{1} Allah, the Exalted, informs that the verses of the Qur'an are {the verses of the Clear Book}; that is, its words and meanings are clear and evident.

{2} Among its clarity and elucidation is that He sent it down in the Arabic tongue, the most noble and clearest of languages, making clear everything people need of beneficial realities. All of this clarification and explanation is {so that you may understand}; that is, so that you may comprehend its limits, its foundations and branches, its commands and prohibitions. When you comprehend that with certainty, and your hearts are characterized by knowing it, that produces the action of the limbs and submission to it. And {so that you may understand} means: your intellects increase through the repeated arrival of these noble, lofty meanings upon your minds, so that you move from one state to states higher and more complete than it.

{3} {We relate to you the best of stories} — this is because of their truthfulness, the smoothness of their expression, and the brilliance of their meanings. {By Our revealing to you this Qur'an}; that is, by what this Qur'an contains, which We revealed to you and with which We favored you over the rest of the prophets, and that is pure grace and kindness from Allah. {And indeed you were, before it, among the unaware} — that is, you did not know what the Book was, nor faith, before Allah revealed it to you, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants.

Having praised what this Qur'an contains of stories, and that they are the best of stories absolutely, such that there is nothing among the stories in any other book like this Qur'an, He mentioned the story of Yusuf, his father, and his brothers, the wondrous and beautiful story, and said:

Know that Allah mentioned that He relates to His Messenger the best of stories in this Book; then He mentioned this story, expanded upon it, and mentioned what took place in it. Thereby it is known that it is a complete, perfect, and beautiful story. Whoever wishes to complete it or beautify it with what is mentioned in the Isra'iliyyat (Israelite narrations) for which no chain of transmission or transmitter is known, most of which are lies, then he is presuming to correct Allah and completing something he claims is deficient. And sufficient for you is a matter that reaches this degree of ugliness. For in the details of this surah, many tafsirs have been filled with falsehoods and abhorrent matters that contradict what Allah has related, in considerable measure. So it is incumbent upon the servant to understand from Allah what He has related, and to leave aside whatever else is not transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ).

{4} Then His saying, Exalted is He: {When Joseph said to his father}: Ya'qub (Jacob) son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim the Friend (of Allah), upon them be blessings and peace. {"O my father, indeed I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."} This dream was a preface to what Joseph, upon him be peace, attained of elevation in this world and the Hereafter. Thus it is when Allah wills a great matter: He sends ahead of it a preface as a preparation for it and a facilitation of its affair, and as readiness for the hardships that will come upon the servant, and as kindness toward His servant and benevolence to him. Ya'qub interpreted it: the sun is his mother, the moon is his father, and the stars are his brothers, and that he would be moved through circumstances until he came to a state in which they would submit to him and prostrate before him, in honor and exaltation. And that this would not occur except through means preceding it: Allah's choosing him, His selecting him, and the completion of His favor upon him through knowledge, action, and establishment in the land. And that this blessing would encompass the family of Ya'qub who prostrated to him, and they would become followers of him in it.

{6} For this reason He said: {And thus will your Lord choose you}; that is, He will select you and prefer you by what He has bestowed upon you of noble qualities and fine virtues. {And teach you the interpretation of narrations}; that is, the interpretation of dreams and the explanation of what true narrations, such as the heavenly books and the like, lead to. {And complete His favor upon you}, in this world and the Hereafter, by giving you good in this world and good in the Hereafter. {As He completed it upon your two fathers before, Ibrahim and Ishaq}, for Allah bestowed upon them great and wide blessings, both religious and worldly. {Indeed your Lord is Knowing, Wise}; that is, His knowledge encompasses things and what the hearts of the servants contain of righteousness and otherwise, and He gives each what His wisdom and praiseworthy judgment require; for He is Wise, placing things in their proper places and setting them in their proper ranks.

So Joseph complied with his father's command and did not inform his brothers of it, but concealed it from them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verses 7–9:

{7} He, may He be exalted, says: {Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers are signs} — that is, lessons and proofs for many good matters — {for those who ask} — that is, for everyone who inquires about them, whether by the tongue of circumstance or by the tongue of speech. For it is those who ask who benefit from the signs and lessons, whereas those who turn away do not benefit from the signs, nor from the narratives and clear proofs.

{8} {When they said} among themselves: {Joseph and his brother} — Benjamin — that is, his full brother; otherwise, they are all brothers — {are more beloved to our father than we, though we are a group} — that is, a band — so how does he prefer the two of them [over us] in love and affection? {Indeed, our father is in clear error} — that is, in evident mistake, in that he prefers them over us without any cause we can see or any matter we witness.

{9} {Kill Joseph or cast him out to some land} — that is, remove him from his father in a distant land where he cannot be able to see him; for if you do one of these two things, {your father's face will be clear for you} — that is, he will be free for you and will turn toward you with compassion and love, for his heart has become so occupied with Joseph that he is not free for you. {And after him you will be a righteous people} — that is, after this deed you will be people who repent to God and seek His forgiveness after your sin. Thus they resolved upon repentance before the sin had come from them, to facilitate the deed, remove its ugliness, and encourage one another.

Rather, reach his removal by casting him {into the depths of the well}, and threaten him that he will not disclose your affair, but rather [present him] as a runaway slave [belonging to you], so that {some of the travellers}, who are heading to a distant place and will keep him there, may pick him up. This speaker was the best of them in his opinion regarding Joseph, the most righteous of them, and the most fearful of God in this matter, for some evil is lighter than other evil, and a light harm may be averted by means of it from a heavier harm. So when they agreed upon this opinion:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verse 11–14:

{11} Meaning: The brothers of Yusuf said, arriving at their aim with their father: {O our father, why do you not entrust us with Yusuf, while we are indeed sincere to him?} That is: why does fear of us regarding Yusuf enter you without any cause or reason, while we are {sincere to him}; that is, we are compassionate towards him, wishing for him what we wish for ourselves.
This indicates that Ya'qub (peace be upon him) would not let Yusuf go with his brothers into the wilderness or the like.

{12} When they removed from themselves the accusation that prevented him from sending him with them, they mentioned to him, regarding Yusuf's interest and the enjoyment that his father loves for him, what necessitates that he permit his sending him with them. So they said: {Send him with us tomorrow, he will frolic and play}; that is, he will roam in the wilderness and enjoy himself, {and indeed we will be his guardians}; that is, we will look after him and protect him from any harm that may intend him.

{13} He answered them with his saying: {Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away}; that is, merely your taking him away grieves me and is hard upon me, because I cannot bear to be parted from him, even for a short time; this is one obstacle to sending him. {And} a second obstacle: {I fear that the wolf may devour him while you are heedless of him}; that is, during your heedlessness of him, because he is young and cannot defend himself against the wolf.

{14} {They said: If the wolf devours him while we are a band}; that is, a group keen to protect him; {indeed, then we would be lost}; that is, there would be no good in us and no benefit to be hoped for from us if the wolf devoured him and overpowered us.
So when they prepared for their father the causes that call for his sending and the removal of the obstacles, he then permitted his sending with them for the sake of his enjoyment.

{15} That is: when Yusuf's brothers took him away after his father had given permission, and they resolved to put him at the bottom of the well (ghayabat al-jubb), as the one among them who spoke earlier had said, and they were able to carry out what they had determined, so they exercised their power over him and threw him into the well. Then God was gentle with him by inspiring him, while he was in that distressing state: ﴿You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive.﴾ That is: there will come a time when you will rebuke them and inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not realize it at that time. In this is good news for him that he will be saved from what he has fallen into, and that God will reunite him with his family and brothers in a manner of honour and of establishing him firmly in the land.

{16} ﴿And they came to their father at night, weeping.﴾ That is, so that their coming was later than their usual custom, and their weeping was a sign for them and evidence of their truthfulness.

{17} So they said, offering an excuse that was false: ﴿O our father, we went off racing one another,﴾ either on foot or by archery and shooting contests, ﴿and we left Yusuf by our belongings,﴾ in order to safeguard him and for his comfort, ﴿and the wolf devoured him,﴾ while we were absent from him and busy racing. ﴿And you will not believe us, even if we were truthful.﴾ That is: they offered this excuse, and it is apparent that you would not believe us, because of the sorrow in your heart over Yusuf and your intense tenderness towards him. {21} That is: when the caravan took him away to Egypt and sold him there, the ruler of Egypt (ʿAzīz of Egypt) bought him. When he bought him, he was pleased with him and charged his wife, saying: ﴿Honor his residence; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾. That is: either he will benefit us as a servant would, with all kinds of service, or we will enjoy him as we enjoy our own children. Perhaps this was because the two of them had no child.

﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land﴾. That is: just as We made it easy for the ruler of Egypt to buy him and to honor him with this honor, We made this a prelude to establishing him in the land by this route.

﴿And that We may teach him the interpretation of events﴾: when he remained with no occupation and no concern other than knowledge, that became one of the causes of his learning much knowledge, including the knowledge of rulings, the science of interpreting dreams, and other things.

﴿And Allah is dominant over His affair﴾. That is: His command, may He be exalted, is executed; no one who seeks to nullify it can nullify it, and no one who seeks to overcome it can overcome it.

﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾: therefore there proceeds from them what proceeds of attempts to contend against Allah's decreed rulings, while they are far more incapable and weaker than that.

{22} That is: "When he reached his maturity" (ashuddah), i.e., the completion of his inner and outer strength, and he became fit to bear the heavy burdens of prophethood and messengership. "We gave him judgment and knowledge": that is, We made him a prophet, a messenger, and a learned man devoted to his Lord (ʿālim rabbānī). "Thus do We reward the good-doers" (al-muhsinīn): those who strive in worshipping the Creator, exerting effort and sincere counsel in it, and who toward the servants of God spend their benefit and show kindness to them. Among the recompense for their goodness, We grant them beneficial knowledge. This indicates that Joseph fulfilled the station of ihsan (excellence in doing good), so God gave him judgment among people, abundant knowledge, and prophethood.

This great trial was greater for Joseph than the trial of his brothers and his patience under it, and greater in reward, because it was patience of choice (ṣabr ikhtiyār) in the presence of many motives for committing the act; so he preferred the love of God over them. As for his trial with his brothers, his patience was patience of compulsion (ṣabr iḍṭirār), like the illnesses and hardships that befall a servant without his choosing, for which he has no refuge except to endure them, willingly or unwillingly.

{23–24} The reason is that Yusuf (peace be upon him) remained honoured in the house of the ʿAzīz, and he possessed such beauty, perfection and splendour that it led to this: ﴿she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him from himself﴾; that is, he was her slave and under her management, and the dwelling was one, so it was easy to carry out the reprehensible act without anyone's awareness or any human perceiving it. ﴿And﴾ the calamity increased when ﴿she locked the doors﴾: the place became empty, and the two of them were secure from anyone entering upon them because the doors were locked. She invited him to herself and said: ﴿Come, [I am] yours﴾; that is, do the reprehensible deed and come to me! Moreover, he was a stranger, and a stranger does not feel the same modesty he would feel when in his own homeland among his acquaintances; he was a captive under her hand, and she was his mistress; she possessed beauty that calls to such things; he was a young unmarried man; and she had threatened him that if he did not do what she commanded she would have him imprisoned or subjected to painful punishment. {39} Then he openly called them to the call, saying: {O two companions of the prison, are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?}; that is, are powerless, weak lords who neither benefit nor harm, neither give nor withhold, and who are scattered among trees, stones, angels, the dead, and other kinds of objects of worship which the polytheists take as gods, are they better, or Allah, who possesses the attributes of perfection, the One in His essence, attributes, and actions? There is no partner for Him in any of that, the Subduer, to whose subjugation and authority all things submit; whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be, and there is no creature but that He holds its forelock.

{40} It is well known that whoever has this description and attributes is better than the scattered deities, which are mere names with no perfection and no power. Whatever other religions there are are not upright, but crooked, leading to every evil. {But most people do not know} the realities of things; otherwise, the difference between worshiping Allah alone without partner and associating others with Him is the clearest and most evident of matters. But because most people lack this knowledge, what occurred among them of shirk occurred. Yusuf, peace be upon him, called the two companions of the prison to worship Allah alone and devote religion to Him. It is possible that they responded and submitted, and thus the blessing was completed upon them; and it is possible that they remained upon their shirk, and so the proof was established against them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verse 42:

{42} That is: {And he said} (Yusuf, peace be upon him) {to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved}: he was the one who saw that he would press wine. {Mention me to your lord}; that is, mention to him my situation and my story, so that perhaps he will have compassion on me and bring me out of what I am in. {But Shaytan caused him to forget the mention of his lord}; that is, Shaytan caused that deliverer to forget the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, and the remembrance of what brings him closer to Him. Among that forgetfulness was his forgetting the mention of Yusuf, who deserved to be rewarded with the utmost goodness; and this was so that Allah might accomplish His command and His decree. {So he remained in prison for several years}: and "bidh'" (several) is from three to nine; for this reason it was said that he remained seven years.

When Allah willed to accomplish His command and to permit Yusuf's release from the prison, He ordained a cause for Yusuf's release, the elevation of his station and the exaltation of his rank, namely the king's dream.

When Allah, the Exalted, willed to bring Yusuf out of the prison, He showed the king this wondrous dream, whose interpretation encompasses the entire nation, so that its interpretation would be at the hand of Yusuf; thus his virtue would become manifest and his knowledge would be made clear, which would be for him an elevation in both abodes. Among the fitting measures is that the king, to whom the affairs of the subjects return, is the one who saw it, because their interests are tied to him. He saw a dream that disturbed him, so he gathered the scholars of his people and the men of judgment among them and said:

{43} "Indeed I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and others withered." That is: seven of the cows were lean (ʿijāf). This is a wonder: the lean ones, whose strength had gone, devoured the seven fat ones that had been at the peak of strength. And "I saw seven green ears of grain," which seven withered ears were devouring. "O chiefs, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions." Because the interpretation of all of them is one and the same, and their meaning is one thing.

{44} They were bewildered and could not find a way to explain it. "They said: 'Confused dreams,'" that is: dreams with no substance and no interpretation. This was a definite claim on their part about what they did not know, and an excuse on their part that was no excuse. Then they said: "And we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams," that is: we interpret only true visions, but dreams that come from Satan or from the soul's own talk, we do not interpret. They combined ignorance, a firm judgment that these were confused dreams, and self-admiration, to the point that they did not say, "We do not know their interpretation!" This is among the matters that are not fitting for people of religion and wisdom. Perhaps his inference that this fertile year would occur, though it was not stated in the king's dream, is because he understood from the [specification] of the seven hard years that the year following them would remove their hardship; and it is known that continuous drought for seven consecutive years is only removed by an exceedingly fertile year, otherwise the specification would have had no benefit.

When the messenger returned to the king and the people, and informed them of Yusuf's interpretation of the dream, they marvelled at it and rejoiced at it with the greatest joy.

{43} "Indeed I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and others withered." That is: seven of the cows were lean (ʿijāf). This is a wonder: the lean ones, whose strength had gone, devoured the seven fat ones that had been at the peak of strength. And "I saw seven green ears of grain," which seven withered ears were devouring. "O chiefs, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions." Because the interpretation of all of them is one and the same, and their meaning is one thing.

{44} They were bewildered and could not find a way to explain it. "They said: 'Confused dreams,'" that is: dreams with no substance and no interpretation. This was a definite claim on their part about what they did not know, and an excuse on their part that was no excuse. Then they said: "And we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams," that is: we interpret only true visions, but dreams that come from Satan or from the soul's own talk, we do not interpret. They combined ignorance, a firm judgment that these were confused dreams, and self-admiration, to the point that they did not say, "We do not know their interpretation!" This is among the matters that are not fitting for people of religion and wisdom. This is also from the subtle kindness of God toward Yusuf (peace be upon him): for if he had interpreted it at the outset, before presenting it to the chiefs of his people and their scholars, and they had been unable to answer, it would not have held that place; but when he presented it to them and they were unable to answer, and the king was intensely concerned about it, Yusuf interpreted it, and it had a great effect upon them.

This is like God's showing the excellence of Adam over the angels through knowledge, after He had asked them and they had not known; then He asked Adam, and he taught them the names of everything, and thereby his excellence increased. And as He displays the excellence of the best of His creation, Muhammad (ﷺ), on the Day of Resurrection, by inspiring the creatures to seek intercession through Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus (peace be upon them), and they excuse themselves from it, then they come to Muhammad (ﷺ), and he says: "I am for it, I am for it," and he intercedes for all creation, and attains that praised station which the first and the last envy him for. Glory be to Him whose subtle kindnesses are hidden and whose conveyance of goodness and benevolence to His chosen and beloved elite is delicate.

{45} "And the one of the two who was saved said" — that is, of the two young men, the one who had seen that he was pressing wine, and whom Yusuf had instructed to mention him to his lord. "And he remembered after a period" — that is, he remembered Yusuf, what had happened to him in interpreting their dreams and what he had instructed him, and knew that he was capable of interpreting this dream after some years had passed. So he said: "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me," to Yusuf, to ask him about it.

{46} They sent him, and he came to him, and Yusuf did not reproach him for forgetting, but listened to what he asked about and answered him. He said: "Yusuf, O truthful one," that is, one who is very truthful in his words and deeds: "Explain to us about seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears and others withered, that I may return to the people so that they may know," for they are eager to know its interpretation, and it has concerned them.

{47} Yusuf interpreted the seven fat cows and the seven green ears as seven fertile years, and the seven lean cows and the seven withered ears as seven years of drought. Perhaps the reason for this, and God knows best, is that fertility and drought depend on tillage: when fertility occurs, crops and fields grow strong, their appearance is good, and their produce increases; drought is the opposite. And cows were generally those on which the land is plowed and by which the fields are irrigated, and ears of grain are the greatest and best of staples. He interpreted them in this way because of the correspondence. So in his interpretation he combined the explanation with an indication of what they would do and prepare, in terms of management during the years of plenty for the years of dearth. He said: "You will sow for seven years in succession," that is, consecutively. "Then what you harvest": from those crops, "leave it in its ear," that is, leave it, for that preserves it better and keeps it further from attention, "except a little of what you eat," that is: manage [also] your eating in these fertile years, and let it be little, so that what you store will be abundant and its benefit and effect will be great.

{50} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the king said﴾ to those around him: ﴿Bring him to me﴾, that is, Yusuf, peace be upon him, that they should bring him out of the prison and present him to the king. When the messenger came to Yusuf and ordered him to appear before the king, he refrained from hastening to leave until his complete innocence was made clear. This was from his patience, his intellect and his perfect judgment. So he said to the messenger: ﴿Return to your lord﴾, meaning the king, ﴿and ask him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands﴾, that is, ask him about their affair and their story, for their matter is clear and manifest. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plotting.﴾

{51} So the king summoned the women and said: ﴿What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf?﴾, that is, what was your situation? Did you see from him anything suspicious? So they cleared him, and ﴿they said: Far be Allah from imperfection! We know of him no evil.﴾ That is, not a little and not a lot. Then the cause on which the accusation was built was removed, and nothing remained except what was with the wife of the ruler. So ﴿the wife of the ruler said: Now the truth has become evident﴾, that is, it has been purified and made clear, after we had attached to him the evil and accusation that necessitated Yusuf's imprisonment. ﴿It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful.﴾ That is, in his statements and in his innocence.

{52} ﴿That﴾, the admission that I have made, that I sought to seduce Yusuf, ﴿is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence.﴾ It is possible that by this she meant her husband, that is: so that he may know that when I admitted that I sought to seduce Yusuf, I did not betray him in his absence; nothing had occurred from me except mere seduction, and I did not corrupt his marital bed. It is also possible that what is meant is: so that Yusuf may know, when I admit it, that I am the one who sought to seduce him, and that he is truthful that I did not betray him in his absence from me. ﴿And that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers.﴾ For every betrayer, his betrayal and his deceit will inevitably return upon himself, and his affair will inevitably become clear.

{53} Then, since in this speech there was a kind of self-praise, and it implied that nothing sinful had occurred from her in the matter of Yusuf, she corrected herself and said: ﴿And I do not acquit myself﴾, that is, of seduction, of desire, of intense eagerness and of scheming in that matter. ﴿Indeed, the soul is ever inclined to evil﴾, that is, it is much given to commanding its owner toward evil, meaning indecency and all other sins, for it is the vehicle of Satan, and through it he enters upon man. ﴿Except those upon whom my Lord has mercy.﴾ So He saves him from his commanding soul, until his soul becomes at rest with its Lord, submissive to the call of guidance and disobedient to the call of destruction. That is not from the soul itself, but from Allah's grace and mercy upon His servant. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ That is, He forgives whoever dares to commit sins and disobedience if he repents and turns back in penitence, and He is Merciful in accepting his repentance and granting him success in righteous deeds.

This is the correct view: that this is the speech of the wife of the ruler and not the speech of Yusuf, since the context is her speech, and Yusuf at that time was in prison and was not present.

So he said to them, ﴿Bring me a brother of yours from your father.﴾ Then he encouraged them to bring him, saying, ﴿Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?﴾ That is, in hospitality and honoring guests.

{60} Then he warned them against not bringing him, saying, ﴿But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, and you shall not come near me.﴾ He knew they were compelled to come to him, and that this would move them to bring him.

{61} They said, ﴿We will seek to persuade our father concerning him.﴾ This indicates that Ya'qub (peace be upon him) was deeply attached to him and could not bear to be parted from him, and that he consoled himself with him after Yusuf. Therefore they needed persuasion to send him with them. ﴿And we will surely do it,﴾ that is, what you have commanded us.

{62} And Yusuf said to his servants (the young men in his service), ﴿Put their merchandise,﴾ that is, the price with which they had bought the provisions from him, ﴿into their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their families, so that they may come back.﴾ Some have said that he did this so they would feel obliged not to keep it. It appears that he intended to encourage them toward his kindness, by measuring for them fully and then returning their goods to them in a way that they would not sense or notice, as will come. Kindness brings a person to fulfill his obligation fully to the one who is kind.

{63} When they returned to their father, they said, ﴿O our father, measure has been withheld from us,﴾ that is, unless you send our brother with us. ﴿So send our brother with us, and we will get measure,﴾ that is, so that this would be the means of our receiving measure. Then they pledged to protect him, saying, ﴿And indeed we will be his guardians,﴾ against anything that might befall him that he would dislike.

{64} He (peace be upon him) said to them, ﴿Shall I trust you with him any more than I trusted you with his brother before?﴾ That is, you had already pledged more than this to protect Yusuf, yet you did not fulfill the solemn commitment you had made. So I do not trust your pledge and your protection, and I trust only in God Most High. ﴿But God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾ That is, He knows my condition, and I hope that He will show mercy to me, guard him, and return him to me. It seems that in these words he had softened toward sending him with them.

{63} When they returned to their father, they said, ﴿O our father, measure has been withheld from us,﴾ that is, unless you send our brother with us. ﴿So send our brother with us, and we will get measure,﴾ that is, so that this would be the means of our receiving measure. Then they pledged to protect him, saying, ﴿And indeed we will be his guardians,﴾ against anything that might befall him that he would dislike.

{64} He (peace be upon him) said to them, ﴿Shall I trust you with him any more than I trusted you with his brother before?﴾ That is, you had already pledged more than this to protect Yusuf, yet you did not fulfill the solemn commitment you had made. So I do not trust your pledge and your protection, and I trust only in God Most High. ﴿But God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾ That is, He knows my condition, and I hope that He will show mercy to me, guard him, and return him to me. It seems that in these words he had softened toward sending him with them.

{65} Then, when they opened their belongings, they found their merchandise had been returned to them. This shows that it was known to them that Yusuf had returned it deliberately, and that he intended to give it to them as their own. They said to their father, to encourage him to send their brother with them, ﴿O our father, what more could we desire?﴾ That is, what could we seek after this beautiful generosity, since he gave us full measure and returned our merchandise to us in this good manner, which reflects sincerity and noble character? ﴿This is our merchandise, returned to us. We will bring provisions for our family, and we will guard our brother, and we will gain an additional camel's load.﴾ That is, if we go with our brother, it will be the cause of his measuring for us, so we will provide for our family and bring them what they need of food. ﴿And we will gain an extra camel's load﴾ by sending him with us, for he gives each person one camel's load. ﴿That is an easy measure,﴾ that is, one that is simple and will cause you no harm, because the period will not be long and the benefit has become clear.

{66} Ya'qub said to them, ﴿I will never send him with you until you give me a solemn covenant from God,﴾ that is, a binding pledge and an oath by God ﴿that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are encircled by disaster,﴾ that is, unless some matter befalls you that you cannot resist or prevent. ﴿When they had given him their solemn pledge,﴾ as he had said and intended, ﴿he said, "God is the Guardian over what we say."﴾ That is, His witness over us and His preservation and guarantee are sufficient for us.

{67} Then, when he had sent him with them, he instructed them that when they entered Egypt they should not enter ﴿from one gate, but enter from different gates.﴾ He feared the evil eye for them because of their number and the splendor of their appearance, since they were the sons of one man. This was the reason, ﴿but I cannot avail you anything against God.﴾ Whatever is decreed must occur. ﴿The command belongs only to God;﴾ that is, the decree is His and the command is His. What He decrees and judges must come to pass. ﴿In Him I have put my trust,﴾ that is, I rely on God and not on the means I have advised you to take. ﴿And let those who trust rely upon Him.﴾ Through reliance on God every desired goal is attained and every feared thing is averted.

{68} When they went and ﴿entered from where their father had commanded them,﴾ that action ﴿did not avail them anything against God, except a need in the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled.﴾ This was an expression of the compassion and love a father has for his children, and so he gained a kind of tranquility and fulfillment of what was in his heart. This is not a deficiency in his knowledge, for he was one of the noble messengers and the godly scholars. For this reason it is said of him, ﴿And indeed he was a possessor of knowledge,﴾ that is, a person of great knowledge, ﴿because of what We had taught him,﴾ that is, by Our teaching him. He comprehended it not by his own power and strength, but by God's grace and instruction. ﴿But most people do not know,﴾ the outcomes of affairs and the subtleties of things. Likewise, even among the people of knowledge, much of its rulings and implications remains hidden from them.

{69} That is: when Yusuf's brothers entered upon Yusuf, "he took his brother to himself" — that is, his full brother, Binyamin, whom he had ordered them to bring and whom he embraced and singled out from among his brothers, and informed him of the true state of affairs. He said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed" — that is, do not grieve "at what they used to do," for the outcome will be good for us. Then he informed him of what he intended to do and of the stratagem by which he would keep him with himself until the matter came to its end.

{70} "So when he had furnished them with their provisions," that is, he measured out for each one of his brothers, including this brother of his, "he placed the drinking-cup" — and it is the vessel from which one drinks and by which one measures — "in his brother's bag. Then" they filled their goods, and when they set off departing, "a caller called out: O caravan, indeed you are thieves." Perhaps this caller did not know the true state of affairs.

{71} "They said" — that is, Yusuf's brothers — "and they turned towards them," to dispel the accusation, for the thief has no concern except to distance himself and depart from the one he stole from, so that his theft may be secure for him; but these came towards them, having no concern except to remove the accusation with which they had been charged. So they said in this situation: "What is it that you are missing?" They did not say, "What did we steal?", because they were certain that they were innocent of theft.

{72} "They said, 'We are missing the king's goblet, and for whoever brings it is a camel's load'" — that is, a reward for him for finding it — "and I am its guarantor" — that is, its surety. This is what the caller who was searching said.

{73} "They said, 'By God, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land,'" through every kind of sin, "and that we were not thieves." This is more emphatic in denying the accusation than if they had said, "By God, we did not corrupt in the land and did not steal."

{74} "They said, 'Then what is its penalty,'" that is, the penalty for this act, "if you are liars?" — namely, if it were found with you.

{75} "They said, 'Its penalty is: whoever is found in his bag, then he himself is its penalty'" — that is, the one found in his bag "is its penalty," by which the owner of the stolen property takes possession of him. {76} So the inspector began with their bags before his brother's bag, in order to dispel the suspicion that it had been placed there deliberately. "Indeed, then" — that is, if we took other than the one in whose bag it was found — "we would be wrongdoers," for we would have placed the punishment in other than its proper place.

{69} That is: when Yusuf's brothers entered upon Yusuf, "he took his brother to himself" — that is, his full brother, Binyamin, whom he had ordered them to bring and whom he embraced and singled out from among his brothers, and informed him of the true state of affairs. He said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed" — that is, do not grieve "at what they used to do," for the outcome will be good for us. Then he informed him of what he intended to do and of the stratagem by which he would keep him with himself until the matter came to its end.

{70} "So when he had furnished them with their provisions," that is, he measured out for each one of his brothers, including this brother of his, "he placed the drinking-cup" — and it is the vessel from which one drinks and by which one measures — "in his brother's bag. Then" they filled their goods, and when they set off departing, "a caller called out: O caravan, indeed you are thieves." Perhaps this caller did not know the true state of affairs.

{71} "They said" — that is, Yusuf's brothers — "and they turned towards them," to dispel the accusation, for the thief has no concern except to distance himself and depart from the one he stole from, so that his theft may be secure for him; but these came towards them, having no concern except to remove the accusation with which they had been charged. So they said in this situation: "What is it that you are missing?" They did not say, "What did we steal?", because they were certain that they were innocent of theft.

{72} "They said, 'We are missing the king's goblet, and for whoever brings it is a camel's load'" — that is, a reward for him for finding it — "and I am its guarantor" — that is, its surety. This is what the caller who was searching said.

{73} "They said, 'By God, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land,'" through every kind of sin, "and that we were not thieves." For theft is among the greatest kinds of corruption in the land. They swore only upon their knowledge that they were neither corrupters nor thieves, because they knew that they had tested their own conduct and found in it what indicates their chastity and piety, and that this matter could not occur from them, by the knowledge of those who accused them. This is more emphatic in denying the accusation than if they had said, "By God, we did not corrupt in the land and did not steal."

{74} "They said, 'Then what is its penalty,'" that is, the penalty for this act, "if you are liars?" — namely, if it were found with you.

{75} "They said, 'Its penalty is: whoever is found in his bag, then he himself is its penalty'" — that is, the one found in his bag "is its penalty," by which the owner of the stolen property takes possession of him. This was in their religion: that when theft was established against a thief, he became the property of the owner of the stolen goods. Hence they said: "Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers."

{76} So the inspector began with their bags before his brother's bag, in order to dispel the suspicion that it had been placed there deliberately. When he did not find it in their bags, "he brought it out from his brother's bag." He did not say, "His brother found it" or "his brother stole it," out of regard for the actual reality. Thereupon Yusuf achieved what he wanted of keeping his brother with him, in a manner his brothers did not perceive. He, exalted is He, said: "Thus did We devise for Yusuf" — that is, We facilitated for him this scheme by which he reached an end that is not blameworthy. "He could not have taken his brother under the king's law," for it was not part of his religion that a thief be taken as property; rather, they had a different penalty for him. Had the judgment been referred to the king's religion, Yusuf would not have been able to keep his brother with him, but he made the ruling be theirs, so that what he wanted might be accomplished. He, exalted is He, said: "We raise in degrees whom We will" — through beneficial knowledge and knowing the paths that lead to their goal, just as We raised the degrees of Yusuf. "And over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows" — so every scholar has above him one who is more knowledgeable than he, until knowledge ends with the One who knows the unseen and the seen.

{77} When Yusuf's brothers saw what they saw, "they said, 'If he steals, then a brother of his before him has stole'" — they meant Yusuf, peace be upon him. Their intention was to absolve themselves, and that this brother and his brother might do what theft entails, and they were not full brothers of ours. In this there is a great deal of disparagement of the two of them. Hence "Yusuf concealed it within himself and did not reveal it to them" — that is, he did not respond to what they said with what they would dislike; rather he swallowed his anger and kept the matter hidden within himself. He "said" within himself: "You are worse in position," for you have accused us of what you yourselves are more deserving of. "And God knows best what you describe" — regarding us, of one who described us with theft, from which God knows we are innocent.

{78} Then they adopted with him the approach of flattery, perhaps he would allow them to have their brother. So "they said, 'O Chief, indeed he has an elderly father, a great old man'" — that is, he cannot bear to be without him, and separation from him will be hard for him. "So take one of us in his place; indeed, we see you are among the good-doers." — so be good to us and to our father by that.

{79} Yusuf said, "God forbid that we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property." That is: it would be an injustice on our part if we took the innocent for the guilt of one with whom we found our property. He did not say, "whoever stole." All of this is a guarding against lying. "Indeed, then" — that is, if we took other than the one in whose bag it was found — "we would be wrongdoers," for we would have placed the punishment in other than its proper place.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 12, verses 80–83:**

{80} That is: when the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) despaired of Yusuf allowing them to take their brother, {they withdrew to confer in private (najiyy)}; that is, they gathered alone, with no one else among them, and began to confer secretly among themselves. {The eldest of them said: "Did you not know that your father had taken a solemn covenant (mawthiq) from you in the name of Allah"}, to bring him back safely, "unless you are encompassed (by misfortune)", {and before that you failed in regard to Yusuf}. So two matters converged upon you: your failure concerning Yusuf in the past, and your not bringing back his brother in the present. Therefore I have no face with which to confront my father. {"So I will not leave this land"}; that is, I will remain in this land and not depart from it, {"until my father gives me leave or Allah judges for me"}; that is, decrees for me to return alone or with my brother, {"and He is the best of judges."}

{81} Then he instructed them what to say to their father, and said: {"Return to your father and say: 'O our father, your son has stolen.'"} That is, he has been accused of theft and taken for it; and it was not possible for us to bring him back to you despite the effort we exerted in that. We bear witness only to what we know, for we did not testify to anything we did not know, since we saw the drinking cup brought out from his baggage. {"And we were not witnesses to the unseen."} That is: had we known the unseen, we would not have been so eager and striven so hard to take him with us, nor would we have given you our pledges and covenants. We did not think the matter would reach what it reached.

{82} {"And ask the town in which we were, and the caravan in which we came"}: if you doubt our words, then inquire about what we have told you. {"And indeed we are truthful."} We did not lie, did not alter, and did not change; rather, this is what actually happened.

{83} When they returned to their father and informed him of this news, his grief intensified, his sorrow redoubled, and he suspected them also in this matter, just as he had suspected them in the first. {He said: "Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you. So patience is most fitting (sabrun jamil)"}; that is, he resorted in this to beautiful patience, which is not accompanied by discontent, by impatient distress, or by complaint to people. Then, when he saw that the matter had grown severe and the distress had reached its limit, he turned to hope for relief, saying: {"Perhaps Allah will bring them all to me"}; that is, Yusuf, Benjamin, and their elder brother who remained in Egypt. {"Indeed, He is the All-Knowing"}: who knows my condition, my need for His relief, His bounty, and my dependence on His kindness; {"the All-Wise"}: who has set a measure for everything and an end for every matter according to what His lordly wisdom requires.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verse 84–86:

{84} That is: Ya'qub (peace be upon him) turned away from his sons after they had told him this news, and his grief and sorrow grew intense. His eyes turned white from the sorrow in his heart and the suppressed anguish that caused him to weep greatly, to the point that his eyes turned white from it. ﴿So he was filled with suppressed grief﴾; that is, his heart was full of intense sorrow. ﴿And he said, "Oh, my grief over Yusuf!"﴾; that is, what had been hidden within him of old concern and enduring longing came to the surface, and this lesser calamity, compared to the first, reminded him of the first calamity.

{85} His sons said to him, marvelling at his condition: ﴿"By Allah, you will not cease remembering Yusuf"﴾; that is, you will not stop remembering Yusuf in all your circumstances, ﴿"until you become consumed"﴾; that is, you become perished, with no movement in you and no ability to speak, ﴿"or you become among those who perish"﴾; that is, you will never stop mentioning him while you are still able to mention him.

{86} Ya'qub said: ﴿"I only complain of my anguish"﴾; that is, of what I pour out of speech, ﴿"and my grief"﴾, which is in my heart. ﴿"To Allah"﴾: alone, not to you nor to any other creature; so say whatever you wish. ﴿"And I know from Allah what you do not know"﴾: that He will return them to me and soothe my eye by reuniting me with them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verses 87–92:

{87} That is: Ya'qub (peace be upon him) said to his sons: ﴿O my sons, go and search for Yusuf and his brother﴾; that is, be eager and diligent in searching for them both. ﴿And do not despair of relief from Allah﴾: for hope compels the servant to strive and exert effort in what he hopes for, while despair compels him to sluggishness and laxity; and the most deserving thing for servants to hope for is Allah's bounty, His kindness, His mercy and His relief. ﴿Indeed, none despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people﴾: for because of their disbelief they consider His mercy remote, while His mercy is far from them; so do not imitate the disbelievers. This indicates that a servant's hope in Allah's mercy and relief is in proportion to his faith.

{88} So they went. When they entered upon Yusuf, they said, humbly pleading to him: ﴿O Chief, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods of little value, so give us full measure and be charitable to us﴾; that is, we and our family have been compelled [by hardship]; ﴿and we have come with goods of little value﴾; that is, goods that are pushed aside and rejected because of their scarcity and their not being accepted in their proper place; ﴿so give us full measure﴾; that is, despite the inadequacy of the payment, and be charitable to us by giving more than what is obligatory. ﴿Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable﴾: with the reward of this world and the Hereafter.

{89} When the matter reached its end and he attained his maturity, Yusuf was greatly moved with tenderness toward them, made himself known to them, and rebuked them, saying: ﴿Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother﴾: as for Yusuf, their action toward him is evident; as for his brother, it is perhaps—and Allah knows best—their saying: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his had stolen before﴾, or that the cause which separated him from his father was themselves, and the original factor that necessitated it. ﴿When you were ignorant﴾: this is a kind of excuse for them due to their ignorance, or a reproach to them since they acted as ignorant people act, though this was not becoming or fitting of them.

{90} They realized that the one addressing them was Yusuf, and they said: ﴿Are you indeed Yusuf?﴾ He said: ﴿I am Yusuf, and this is my brother; Allah has bestowed favor upon us﴾: with faith, piety and establishment in this world, and that is due to patience and piety. So ﴿indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient﴾; that is, fears Allah by avoiding what He has forbidden and is patient over pains and calamities and over the commands by carrying them out. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾: for this is part of good conduct, and Allah does not waste the reward of one who does good deeds.

{91} ﴿They said, "By Allah, certainly Allah has preferred you over us﴾; that is, He has favored you over us with noble character and praiseworthy traits, while we wronged you to the utmost and were eager to inflict harm upon you and to separate you from your father; so Allah the Exalted preferred you and empowered you to do what you wished [and indeed we were wrongdoers. This is the utmost acknowledgment from them of the sin they committed against Yusuf].

{92} Yusuf (peace be upon him) said to them, out of generosity and magnanimity: ﴿No reproach will there be upon you today﴾; that is, I will not reproach or blame you, ﴿Allah will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful﴾. He granted them complete pardon without reproaching them for the earlier sin, and he prayed for them for forgiveness and mercy. This is the ultimate of kindness, which comes only from the elite of creation and the best of the chosen ones.

{98} ﴿He said﴾ responding to their request and hastening to answer them: ﴿I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ My hope in Him is that He will forgive you, have mercy on you, and envelop you in His mercy.
It has been said that he delayed asking forgiveness for them until the virtuous time of dawn, so that it would be more complete as a plea for forgiveness and closer to being answered.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verses 99–100:

{99} That is: {So when} Ya'qub (Jacob) and his children and all their family prepared and set out from their land, intending to reach Yusuf in Egypt and settle there. When they arrived to him and {entered upon Yusuf, he drew his parents close to him}; that is, he embraced them, singled them out for closeness to himself, and showed them great kindness, goodness, honour and respect. {And he said} to all his family: {Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security}: safe from every hardship and fear. So they entered in this joyful state, and their weariness and the hardship of living were removed from them, and happiness and delight came to them.

{100} {And he raised his parents onto the throne}; that is, onto the royal couch and the seat of the ruler (al-'Aziz). {And they fell down before him in prostration}; that is, his father, his mother and his brothers prostrated in a manner of glorification, honour and reverence. {And he said}, when he saw this state and saw their prostration to him: {O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream from before}: when he saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon prostrating to him. This is its fulfilment, to which it has come and reached. {My Lord has made it true}: He did not make it into confused dreams. {And He has been good to me}: a great goodness, {when He took me out of the prison and brought you from the desert}: and this is from His gentleness and the beauty of His address, peace be upon him, in that he mentioned his state in the prison and did not mention his state in the well, for the completeness of his pardon of his brothers and that he does not mention that sin. And that your coming from the desert is from Allah's kindness to me. He did not say "He brought you from hunger and hardship," nor did he say "He was good to you," but he said "He was good to me," making the goodness return to himself. So blessed is He who singles out for His mercy whom He wills of His servants, and bestows upon them from Himself mercy; indeed He is the Bestower. {After Satan had caused discord between me and my brothers}: he did not say "Satan caused discord between my brothers," but it was as though the sin and ignorance came from both sides. So praise be to Allah, who humiliated Satan and drove him away, and gathered us after that arduous separation. {Indeed my Lord is Subtle in what He wills}: He conveys His kindness and goodness to the servant from where he does not perceive, and brings him to lofty stations through matters he dislikes. {Indeed He is the All-Knowing}: who knows the outward and inward aspects of matters and the secrets and hearts of His servants. {The All-Wise}: in placing things in their proper places and driving affairs to their appointed times.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 12, verse 102:

{102} When Allah had related this story to Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah said to him: {That} [the news] which We have informed you of is {among the news of the unseen} which, had We not revealed it to you, this noble report would not have reached you, for you were not present {with them when they agreed upon their plan} — that is, the brothers of Joseph. {While they were scheming} against him, when they conspired to separate him from his father, in a situation that none knows except Allah the Exalted, and that no one can come to know except through Allah's teaching it to him, just as Allah the Exalted said when He related the story of Moses and what happened to him, mentioning the circumstance that no path exists for creation to know except through His revelation, saying: {And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses...} [28:44] — the verses. {103} God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And most of the people, even if you were eager, would not be believers﴾ in their faith, for their perceptions and aims have already become corrupt; so the eagerness of those who advise them does not benefit them, even if the obstacles were removed, such that they teach them and call them to what is good for them and to averting evil from them, without any wage or return, and even if they produced for them whatever proofs and signs indicating their truthfulness they could produce.

{104} For this reason He said: ﴿And you do not ask them for any wage for it. It is only a reminder to the worlds﴾, by which they remember what benefits them, so that they may do it, and what harms them, so that they may abandon it.

{105} ﴿And how many a sign there is in the heavens and the earth that they pass by﴾, indicating to them the oneness of God, ﴿while they turn away from it﴾.

{106} Despite this, if some faith is found among them, still ﴿most of them do not believe in God without associating others with Him﴾. They, although they acknowledge God's lordship and that He is the Creator, the Provider, and the Manager of all affairs, nevertheless associate others with Him in His divinity and His oneness.

{107} Those who have reached this state have nothing left but that punishment should descend upon them and retribution should seize them while they are secure. For this reason He said: ﴿Then do they feel secure﴾, meaning: those who commit those deeds and turn away from the signs of God, ﴿that an overwhelming punishment from God will come upon them﴾, meaning: a punishment that covers them, encompasses them, and uproots them; ﴿or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly﴾, meaning: unexpectedly, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾. Indeed, they have deserved that; so let them repent to God and abandon what would be a cause of their punishment.
